simple.meaning: אֲבַד (ʼăbad) is a Hebrew action word meaning “destroy, perish.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 7 times in Jeremiah, Daniel, beginning at Jeremiah 10:11. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֲבַד (H7) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: אֲבַד (ʼăbad) / H7 is traced through Jeremiah 10:11, Daniel 2:12, Daniel 2:18, Daniel 2:24 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’ ”
Because of this, the king was angry and very furious, and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
that they would desire mercies of the God of heaven concerning this secret; that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
